references.text: The Amorites pursued the Israelites and struck them down, just as the men of Ai had pursued and struck down the Israelites.
The Lord warned that Israel would be defeated by their enemies if they were disobedient to Him, which is what happened at Ai.
A heart melting with fear is part of the curse for disobedience, as occurred with the people after the defeat at Ai.
Rahab described how the hearts of the Canaanites melted with fear before Israel, but here it is the hearts of Israel that melt with fear.
Previously, the hearts of the Amorites melted with fear before Israel, but now the roles have been reversed following the defeat at Ai.
The spies underestimated Ai and recommended only two or three thousand men, which led to their defeat.
The prophet Isaiah uses the same image of hearts melting like water when facing judgment and defeat.
The psalmist describes a heart melting like wax, the same image of fear and discouragement found in Joshua 7:5.
